title: Continuation Credit after an Earlier Exception Approval Has Run Out (Formulary Benefit)
content:
Under the Formulary Benefit, a continuation credit is added to the exigency period of an expedited exception approval for a member whose earlier exception approval for the drug has run out. The member's exception history is read for approvals of the drug and their expiration dates. The date that counts is the latest expiration date among those approvals.

**Clause.**
1. An approval of an exception for the drug is on record, and its latest expiration date has passed (it is before the handling date) fewer than **3** whole months before the handling date. The recent-approval credit of **5** days is added.
2. Such an approval is on record, and its latest expiration date passed longer ago, 3 whole months or more. The older-approval credit of **2** days is added.
3. In every other case, no continuation credit is added. This covers a member with no approval for the drug on record, and one whose latest approval has not yet expired.

The credit is added to the exigency period before the floor of one day is applied.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical handling date of 20 August)

| Latest expiration of an approval for the drug | Whole months since | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| 19 August | 0 | 5 days |
| 21 May | 2 | 5 days |
| 20 May | 3 | 2 days |
| 20 August or later (not yet expired) | | nothing |
| no approval on record | | nothing |
